answer: Radio witness seats (Helium-style proof of coverage): each ID binds to one LoRa hotspot at a stated spot, say a lagoon-side wharf. Every 6 h the beacon has it broadcast a signed chirp, and at least 3 other IDs' hotspots 2-20 km away must hear it (proposed). A falcon-eyed check compares reported signal strength against distance: 20 IDs claiming different towns but heard by the same witnesses at near-identical RSSI are one rig and share one seat. Measured today: 41 seats; spoof rate unmeasured until a pilot runs.
